key_insight: AEGIS is a comprehensive benchmark that reveals substantial blind spots in current forensic tools: even advanced models (e.g., GPT-5.1) achieve only 48.80% overall detection and expert methods show limited localization (IoU 30.09%).
problem_solved: Provides a domain-specific, fine-grained evaluation suite for forensic analysis of AI-generated academic images, exposing realistic forensic difficulty across diverse academic image types and forgery modes.
method: Curate a multi-domain dataset covering 7 academic categories and 39 fine-grained subtypes to capture domain-specific complexity.
Simulate four prevalent forgery modalities (diverse, realistic manipulations) and define joint detection + localization tasks with standardized metrics (accuracy, IoU).
Benchmark state-of-the-art detectors and generative models to establish baselines and analyze failure modes across categories and attack types.
impact: AEGIS gives AI/ML practitioners a practical, rigorous testbed to measure and improve detection and localization of AI-generated academic imagery, guiding development of more robust forensic models and integrity tools.
visual_elements: Bar chart comparing model detection accuracy across categories (highlighting 48.80% overall).
Heatmap/matrix of localization IoU by category and subtype (showing concentrated low-IoU areas near 30.09%).
Side-by-side examples: original vs. forged image vs. predicted localization mask for each forgery type.
Hierarchy diagram of the 7 categories and 39 subtypes to show dataset breadth and domain specificity.
paper_title: AEGIS: A Holistic Benchmark for Evaluating Forensic Analysis of AI-Generated Academic Images
paper_authors: Bo Zhang, Tzu-Yen Ma, Zichen Tang, Junpeng Ding, Zirui Wang
